question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}{[-\frac{1}{x}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}(-\frac{1}{2}-(-1))\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\text{d}y & =\frac{1}{2}[\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y]_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\pi }{6}-0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{12}\end{aligned}
$$
